prose.summary: The hardwood bedroom furniture qualifies for the CEPA rate under the India-UAE CEPA. This means the reduced duty rate of 12.5% can be claimed, providing an estimated saving of 7500.00 AED.
prose.classification: The tariff line is 94036000 for other wooden furniture, and Mansha's confidence in this classification is high. However, you should confirm the code with Indian customs or a customs broker before shipping.
prose.duty: Under the India-UAE CEPA, the normal (MFN) rate is 20% and the CEPA rate is 12.5%. Claiming the CEPA rate provides an estimated saving of 7500.00 AED.
prose.origin: The rule of origin requires a change in tariff heading (CTH) and value addition (VA) of at least 40%. CTH means non-originating inputs must be classified in a different 4-digit heading than the product, and VA is the share of the product's price that does not come from non-originating materials. The product meets the rule because the final manufacture and minimal operations checks passed, all non-originating inputs are classified outside heading 9403, and the value addition is 52.0% on a FOB basis, which exceeds the 40% threshold.

notes.text: UAE law sets a shorter 3-year minimum for record keeping, but the CEPA's 5-year requirement governs CEPA claims.
The issuing authority may apply risk management, including asking for detailed cost sheets and visiting the factory.
The factory is declared in a free zone: likely not eligible for the ministry's factory registration; confirm with the ministry.
Operations and final manufacture are the exporter's own declaration.
'+' in the rule is read as 'and' (both tests must pass); the agreement does not define '+', so this is Mansha's interpretation.
The duty estimate is on the shipment value given; India charges duty on the assessable (CIF) value at import, so actual amounts will differ.
CEPA rates reduce Basic Customs Duty (BCD) only; IGST, GST compensation cess, the Social Welfare Surcharge (SWS) and any anti-dumping or safeguard duty still apply.
The CEPA rate applies only if the product qualifies under the rules of origin and a valid certificate of origin is presented.
'Direct labour cost' and 'direct overhead cost' are not defined in the agreement.
The agreement does not say whether the build-down and build-up methods use the same threshold, apart from the 5-point Ex-Works adjustment.

No official page read names the Ministry of Foreign Trade as the issuer of the India CEPA certificate specifically: its service page covers preferential certificates in general, and the India-specific page is still on moet.gov.ae.

A producer in a free zone is likely not eligible for Factory Registration, because it requires a factory outside a free zone, and registration is needed before applying for the certificate of origin for India; confirm with the Ministry of Economy and Tourism.
The Social Welfare Surcharge (SWS) is likely charged on the reduced BCD (no CEPA-specific text on it was found).
Anti-dumping and safeguard duties likely still apply (no CEPA exemption from them was found).
UAE law sets a shorter 3-year minimum for record keeping; the CEPA's 5 years governs CEPA claims.
The issuing authority may apply risk management, including asking for detailed cost sheets and visiting the factory.
